title: Shrinking a supporting open in the explicit graph comparison
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and use ordinary unbounded small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Fix $f:X\to Y$, a compactification $c$, and a proper/open/proper presentation $s=(a,e,p)$ [def-pur-etale-graph-presentation-maps]. Let $a':X\to W$ be proper, $v:W\hookrightarrow U_s$ and $e':W\hookrightarrow P_s$ open immersions, with $v a'=a$ and $e v=e'$. Let $t=(a',e',p)$ be the resulting presentation of $f$. Write $R_g=Rg_*$ and $J_j=Dj_!$. Define $S:F_s\to F_t$ by the inverse triangle isomorphism $R_a\to J_vR_{a'}$ of the Cartesian identity-top proper/open square [lem-pur-etale-proper-open-exchange-cube], followed by the canonical open compositor $J_eJ_v\cong J_{e'}$ [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], under $R_p$. Then the specified product/intersection graph comparisons [lem-sf-etale-locally-closed-graph-model] satisfy $S B_{s,c}=B_{t,c}$. The proper ambient scheme is fixed. No quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Substitute he so e′ = v ≫ s.e. Expand each specified graph comparison as graphSide₁ ≪≫ graphMiddle ≪≫ graphSide₂.symm, retaining all associators. Equality-induced open congruence for rfl is the identity.

Prove the side-square calculation directly in the private side_square_pasting lemma. Let D_H have proper edges q,p and open edges b,e; let D_v have proper edges q′,q and open edges rho,v. The smaller side square is their horizontal pasting (with the pullback squares flipped). Let E be the identity-top graph square with proper edges s′,s and bottom rho. Its vertical pasting with D_v is the triangle Q_v. Extract the Cartesian normalization, vertical law and horizontal law from etaleProperOpenExchangeCube. Vertical pasting expresses the Q_v triangle as the inverse compositor for s′,q′, the D_v exchange, the E triangle under Rq, and the compositor for s,q. Remove extension by the identity using naturality of the latter compositor. Invert and cancel the E triangle and compositor. Horizontal pasting expresses the smaller side exchange through D_v and D_H. Naturality of the open compositor cancels its inverse, and naturality of the D_H exchange moves the inverse E triangle through it. The two paths coincide by the preceding vertical equation. This proves an objectwise identity for any such two Cartesian squares and proper graph lifts, without using any final graph comparison or side-pasting theorem.

Specialize side_square_pasting to the two second graph neighborhoods and graphNeighborhoodShrink. Their Cartesian squares, graph factorization and ambient-open equation are supplied by the neighborhood geometry; their proper projection identities are pullback.lift_snd. Whisker the objectwise identity by the fixed outer proper direct image. Naturality of its compositor moves the two components of the shrinking map past that compositor. Expanding the side words gives graphSide₂(s) followed by graphNeighborhoodTriangle equal to etaleGraphShrinkInterchange followed by graphSide₂(s.shrink).

Use etaleGraphShrinkMiddlePasting for the middle words. The fully proved private shrink_cancel postcomposes the desired comparison with the smaller second-side isomorphism, substitutes the side equation, cancels the old second side, substitutes the middle equation and cancels the first-side isomorphism. Reassemble the specified graph comparisons to obtain exactly the unchanged theorem.

theorem etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen_openShrink
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f)
    (s : EtaleGraphPresentation f) {W : Scheme.{u}}
    (a' : X ⟶ W) [IsProper a'] (v : W ⟶ s.U) [IsOpenImmersion v]
    (e' : W ⟶ s.P) [IsOpenImmersion e']
    (ha : a' ≫ v = s.a) (he : v ≫ s.e = e') :
    let t : EtaleGraphPresentation f := {
      U := W
      P := s.P
      a := a'
      e := e'
      p := s.p
      fac := by
        calc
          a' ≫ e' ≫ s.p = (a' ≫ v) ≫ s.e ≫ s.p := by
            rw [← he]
            simp only [Category.assoc]
          _ = f := by rw [ha]; exact s.fac }
    etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen A c s ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerRight
          (rightDerivedLowerStarCompOpenImmersionLowerShriekIso A a' v s.a ha).symm _ ≪≫
        Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _ ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight
            ((mapDerivedCategoryOpenImmersionLowerShriekComp
                (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) v s.e).symm ≪≫
              mapDerivedCategoryOpenImmersionLowerShriekCongr (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) he) _) =
      etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen A c t

old_proof.text: Put T = P_s ×_Y c.Z. Put O_0 = T ×_(c.Z) X, O = T ×_(P_s) U_s and O' = T ×_(P_s) W. Define rho:O'→O by pullback.lift fst (snd≫v), using he. Define kappa:O_0×_T O'→O_0×_T O by pullback.lift fst (snd≫rho). The pullback projection equations and ha show that the old and new first graph lifts agree, and that the new second and intersection graph lifts compose with rho and kappa to the old ones. IsPullback.of_right applied to the two defining pullbacks shows that rho is the base change of v. All these maps are open. Properness of the graph lifts follows by proper-to-separated from their proper projections.

Write H_0,H_1,H_1' for the graph functors on the three supporting neighborhoods, including the exterior R(T→Y)_*. Write K,K' for the intersection graph functors. Let sigma_0:H_0→K and sigma_1:H_1→K be the inverse triangle maps followed by open composition; define sigma_0',sigma_1' on the smaller intersection. Let tau:H_1→H_1' and delta:K→K' be the analogous shrinking maps for rho and kappa. Horizontal normalized proper/open pasting for the nested intersection inclusions, after canonical open composition, gives sigma_0 delta = sigma_0' and sigma_1 delta = tau sigma_1'. The identity-top squares are Cartesian because the lower open arrows are monic, so Cartesian normalization identifies these maps with the upstream triangle isomorphisms.

Let A_0:F_c→H_0, A_1:F_s→H_1, A_1':F_t→H_1' be the graph side words. Write D_H,D_S for the Cartesian side squares with upper open edges b_H:O→T and b_S:O'→T and lower edges e and e'. Let D_v be the Cartesian square with top rho, bottom v and proper vertical neighborhood projections. Let E be the identity-top graph square with lower edge rho. Then D_S is D_v pasted horizontally before D_H, whereas the original triangle Q_v is E stacked vertically above D_v. Apply the horizontal law to D_v,D_H and the vertical law to E,D_v. Cancel the common Gamma(D_v), and use naturality to move Gamma(E) past Gamma(D_H). Including the fixed proper and open compositors, this gives A_1 tau = S A_1'. This does not stack Q_v directly over D_H, whose boundary edges would not match. The identity direct-image word in A_0 is unchanged.

Expand B_s = A_0 sigma_0 sigma_1^(-1) A_1^(-1) and B_t = A_0 sigma_0' (sigma_1')^(-1) (A_1')^(-1), retaining the functor associators. From the side equation obtain A_1^(-1) S = tau (A_1')^(-1). From sigma_1 delta = tau sigma_1' obtain sigma_1^(-1) tau = delta (sigma_1')^(-1). Substitution and sigma_0 delta = sigma_0' give B_s S = B_t. These are cancellation equations between natural isomorphisms, not an equality inferred from their endpoints. The proof applies also to identity and empty opens and requires no quasi-compactness.
